scope: A dated evidence map comparing the Commons LDA/TITAN device-control architecture with four current realtime audio or voice-agent platforms across seven buyer-relevant dimensions.
comparison_boundary: This is not a ranking: Commons LDA/TITAN is a device-control agent, while the external systems are realtime audio APIs or voice-agent platforms. Claims are comparable evidence cells, not proof of substitutability or superiority.
commercial_use: Use this map to scope sponsored benchmarks, integration work, joint reproductions, and private evaluations around measured device actuation, realtime conversation, telephony, recovery, and durable evidence gaps.

systems.evidence_scope: Current Commons source plus exact public live-emulator receipts at the generated-from commit; no physical-phone or production-customer inference.

interruption.statement: During a task, the foreground service checks growing offline-Vosk partials for a bare or addressed stop/cancel/abort/halt command and routes it to the task stop path.
interruption.limitations: The source says the check is immediate/for speed, but this map has no measured stop-to-halt latency distribution.

source.evidence_phrase: halts the agent immediately (checked on partial results for speed).

latency.statement: The architecture document reports about 28-31 decode tokens per second on the Fold and about 2-4 seconds of think time for a small JSON action, with pipelining and deterministic precondition checks intended to hide some wait.
latency.limitations: These are repository-reported design figures, not a fresh benchmark, percentile distribution, or provider-comparable end-to-end voice latency measurement.

source.evidence_phrase: a step is ~ 2-4 s of think.

tool_use.statement: A headless AOSP API 34 proof installed the owner LDA, observed through the native accessibility snapshot, clicked native element 1, and recorded a changed semantic digest.
tool_use.limitations: This proves one emulator observe/click transition, not arbitrary-app completion, physical-phone deployment, telephony, or a production success rate.

source.evidence_phrase: live native click on LDA element

recovery.statement: The documented handset design intentionally has no boot persistence; a reboot stops the agent, while task history and logs persist separately for review.
recovery.limitations: No live application-session resume after reboot or process death is claimed here; emulator cold-boot repair is infrastructure recovery, not task resumption.

source.evidence_phrase: No boot persistence.

receipts.statement: TaskHistory stores monotonic run IDs, objective, outcome, plan, executed steps, per-step ratings, duration, failure class, build, and timestamp; Commons adds immutable Git receipts around selected live proofs.
receipts.limitations: The on-device history is bounded local state and is not itself an independently replicated or customer-accepted delivery receipt.

source.evidence_phrase: task log is the owner's record of what the agent DID

deployment_boundary.statement: The architecture is an Android foreground service using an imported local Gemma LiteRT-LM model, accessibility perception/actuation, Vosk wake-word audio, and device-local UI surfaces.
deployment_boundary.limitations: The current exact live proof is an isolated x86_64 emulator override; the normal owner APK is arm64 and no physical phone was touched in that receipt.

source.evidence_phrase: Current (working): `Gemma 4 E2B`

data_handling.statement: The repository describes on-demand screen reads only during active tasks, local Vosk wake-word processing, and a fully local LLM; it also documents an explicit optional cloud command-recognition mode elsewhere.
data_handling.limitations: This is a source-level architecture statement, not a captured network trace or independent privacy audit, and the optional cloud speech path changes the boundary when selected.

source.evidence_phrase: screen or audio - ever leaves the device
